name: Department of Renaming Things
desc: The meeting hall has a patriotic new name. Your form uses the old one; the amendments use both. The clerk identifies the building by pointing through the window.

choices.label: Read everything; use a snack pack

effects.log: Snacks gone, instructions matched and saved. You've traced the hall all the way across the street.
Two corrections missed. You confidently prepare to visit the building formerly known as the building.
You miss a cross-reference. Six people, six answers. The form has successfully created a committee.

name: The Efficiency Emergency
desc: The council lists five accomplishments from firing the bridge crew. All five mean “fired the bridge crew.” The bridge is closed; former workers need help hauling detour signs.

choices.label: Donate one pack; haul barrier signs

effects.log: Supplies donated, arms aching. You haul the signs without once calling yourselves job creators.
You file the dated photo. It shows exactly how much traffic “efficiency” can carry: none.

name: Civic Center Potluck
desc: The notice canceling the federal food fund is taped beside the stew. 'Printouts go under the bowls,' says the cook. 'That's the federal contribution.'

effects.log: You eat and pack three bundles. Somebody offers seconds without checking whether you're a corporation.

choices.label: Pack two bundles; share their story

effects.log: You promise to mention the cooks in Washington. They label the leftovers 'evidence.'
Your beans join the pantry. The cook offers naming rights to one very unimpressed potato.

name: Crossing Block Party
desc: After the order to cut federal library support, librarians stage a cookout: free books, free seating. 'I know,' one says. 'This is how empires fall.'

choices.label: Give one food bundle; help grill

effects.log: You grill while a librarian reads horror aloud. The horror is next year's budget.
'I shouldn't need a muffin mortgage to sit down.' The café workers in line howl.

choices.label: Share two water and towel bundles

effects.log: You pass out cold towels. The librarian saves one for the next official who works up a sweat attacking free books.

name: Freeway Mural Crew
desc: Artists under an overpass named for a billionaire are painting his cleaner. They need help, water and a group photo. His contribution to the portrait is the muddy footprint she’s scrubbing.

effects.log: Arms aching, you finish a coat. The billionaire's sign contributes its usual share of the labor.
Your contribution fits in the photo without its own dedication plaque.
All six of you squeeze into the photo. The billionaire’s name stays above everyone’s head. Even the overpass has an org chart.

name: Mail Drop Pickup
desc: A volunteer brings letters mocking Washington’s five-accomplishment demand, a road pack, and a request to record yours. One retiree lists ‘fed the cat’ twice. The cat requests a third.

effects.log: You save the letters, laughing. The cat's performance-management system is just as arbitrary, but considerably fluffier.
Update recorded, road pack collected. Your next five accomplishments will be performed with your mouth full.

choices.label: Sort urgent letters; share one pack

effects.log: One snack pack fuels sorting. Someone labels the empty wrapper “Employee of the Month.”

name: Who Gets to Say ‘No Comment’?
desc: At a free protest workshop, a radio host rehearses questions about the cabinet’s Signal chat. She says ‘I don’t know’ is acceptable. Nobody from customer service believes her.

effects.log: Transcript checked. Your answer survives a follow-up question without blaming the microphone.
One does a flawless cabinet impression: talks for two minutes, answers nothing, requests a promotion.

name: Pop-up Mutual Aid
desc: Three volunteers offer $10 and a food bundle for loading. Since the federal food-funding cuts, the folding table is the only one that hasn’t worked a double.

choices.label: Give two bundles; share their appeal

effects.log: You film the food being unloaded. Your financial transparency report comes with dented cans.

choices.label: Load for $10 and one food bundle

effects.log: Dinner, ten dollars, and a backache. Management is a folding chair. You prefer it.

choices.label: Give one bundle; post their wishlist

effects.log: You share the wishlist. It contains beans, rice, and no exciting opportunities for private equity.

name: Mutual Aid Dispatch Center
desc: Food-aid drivers borrow radios to coordinate deliveries after the federal food fund is canceled. Washington cut the money; the loading schedule still says 'ask Kevin.'

choices.label: Deliver two food bundles in your van

effects.log: You make both drop-offs. Nobody commissions a feasibility study of the front steps.

choices.label: Donate one bundle of radio batteries

effects.log: The radio crackles back. Kevin announces 'We have beans.' Something worth a national address.

choices.label: Keep a copy of the needs tally

effects.log: You keep the tally for Washington. Kevin has listed every shortage. 'Nobody could have known' will have to explain page two.

name: The Street Formerly Known as the Street
desc: One street, three official names. Residents offer directions, public help numbers, and a road pack for moving their corrected map board. The pizza driver is touring the town’s entire patriotic history.

effects.log: Numbers checked and saved. You can now ask “Where are we?” without first hearing about the mayor’s accomplishments.

choices.label: Move the board; correct the arrows

effects.log: Sore arms, one road pack earned. The arrows point somewhere besides the mayor's achievements.
You find the exit. The crew celebrates like somebody's successfully canceled a subscription.

name: Overpass Pop-Up Stage
desc: An overpass troupe stages the federal library cuts. Their billionaire is a sock puppet. 'We tried a real billionaire,' the director says. 'Couldn't afford the subsidies.'

effects.log: You post the show. The sock puppet has better comic timing and fewer conflicts of interest.
You question the puppet until hoarse. He demands security. The director shuts him in a sock drawer.

name: Forecast: Still Your Problem
desc: A reporter asks about Sharpiegate and bosses denying weather. You remember being told the roads were fine because the store was open. The register must control the jet stream.

choices.label: Answer with the saved weather alerts

effects.log: You cross-check every date, exhausted. The storm had issued clearer instructions than your shift manager.

choices.label: Send a short account while resting

effects.log: Feet up, you send two sentences. The passenger seat offers better accommodation than your old employer.

choices.label: Record an interview; verify the dates

effects.log: You save the verified recording. The warning said ‘stay home.’ Payroll’s version had different weather.

name: An Interview, Between Refills
desc: A diner reporter asks to record your trip costs and mileage. You agree. The cabinet gave a journalist airstrike plans without even checking the guest list.

choices.label: Answer with receipts on the table

effects.log: You check every total, exhausted. The reporter asks if you bought breakfast or the diner.
Quick, painless, wrong. The reporter checks the map. Your estimate has driven farther than the van.

choices.label: Let a crewmate talk; stretch out

effects.log: They take the questions. You become the first person in a political interview to lie down openly.

name: College Radio Phonebank
desc: The college station needs spots opposing the federal library cuts. Eight dollars per recording. Your opinion has reached the market value of a sandwich.

effects.log: 'Free Wi-Fi scares billionaires,' you tell listeners. 'People might read the second half of the contract.'

choices.label: Share one snack bundle; rehearse calls

effects.log: You pass out snacks and rehearse calls. The script contains fewer apologies than your work emails.
You record the spot and pocket eight dollars. Your unpaid opinions are filing a grievance.

name: Service Station Handoff
desc: The tariff quote has promoted replacement parts to luxury goods. A union mechanic and apprentices offer to fit your spares. “Congratulations. Your wipers are now an inheritance.”

effects.log: Your spares go in; you rest. The waiting-room chair delivers the recovery Washington advertised.
The apprentices record the symptoms. The van receives more oversight than the tariff plan.
Wipers fitted. You can see the road again. The economic outlook remains streaky.

name: Union Solidarity Blockade
desc: Tariff uncertainty halved the shifts. The CEO's bonus somehow retained full-time hours. A steward offers space on the picket and a box of donated road snacks.

effects.log: You raise your signs. Management reports a troubling rise in employee engagement.
The steward passes up a road pack. The outside agitators are now carrying snacks.
You open the snacks. The picket's first shareholder meeting distributes actual crackers.

name: Water Drive Relay
desc: Drivers offer two supply bundles for unloading beneath Trump’s showerhead headline. 'He needs more pressure,' says a courier. 'My boss texts every time my GPS dot stops.'

effects.log: Drivers refill their bottles. Your water policy has passed its first test: containing water.
Two bundles earned. Your arms object to being classified as critical infrastructure.

name: One Socket, Six Phones
desc: Tariffs have hiked charger prices. Six phones share one overheating adapter. A repair volunteer checks your spares. “Too small to bail out. We’ll have to fix it.”

effects.log: The adapter gets replaced; you get a chair. Neither requires a Senate hearing.
Your neck aches over the last charged phone. The other five enjoy tariff protection from electricity.

choices.label: Use two repair packs; document costs

effects.log: Fix completed, price notice saved. At last, a rising percentage that isn’t on a price tag.

name: Carry This to Washington
desc: Library volunteers hand you public records for Washington, with private details removed. Their security system is a folder labeled ‘PUBLIC.’ The cabinet should ask about the enterprise plan.

effects.log: Sources checked, folder packed. Washington’s homework rides on the floor. It didn’t chip in for gas.
Their private copies get separate folders marked ‘PRIVATE.’ The cabinet is welcome to steal this technology.
You catch a phone number in the public copy. One stroke of a pen; no press conference explaining how secure the pen is.

name: The Rally Address Has Entered the Chat
desc: The rally has two addresses in your chat. To improve security after Signal, someone changes the icon to a padlock. Both addresses are now securely wrong.

choices.label: Check and share the organizer’s notice

effects.log: You confirm the address and send the dated link. The padlock gets promoted to decoration.
You date the screenshots: wrong town, wrong year. Your phone now needs a cigarette.
Your directions send a friend to an empty parking lot. Congratulations on organizing a deeply private rally.

name: Please Hold While We Check Reality
desc: At a free protest workshop, a volunteer hands out the Sharpiegate report, then plays Trump arguing with a forecast. Six workers recognize the problem: somebody gave the difficult customer nuclear weapons.

effects.log: Your answers match the report. Your patience runs out when ‘the president’ asks to speak to the weather’s manager.
You rehearse ‘Show me where it says that.’ Nobody offers the imaginary president a refill.

choices.label: Send remembered notes; take a nap

effects.log: Excellent nap. Incorrect summary. The report has your correction waiting when you wake, like a shift supervisor.

name: The Public Paper Pile
desc: Residents offer cut notices beside DOGE's corrected contract figure. Eight billion became eight million. Their closed service desk has declined to reopen by typo.

choices.label: Sort and save the dated notices

effects.log: Head aching, you file the notices. “Savings” takes three folders; “service” fits under CLOSED.
Copies mailed. Washington’s savings plan is now eating into your envelope stash.

choices.label: Store the files; close the folder

effects.log: Files saved, folder closed. By DOGE standards, you’ve now eliminated all the paperwork.

name: Private Chat, Public Application
desc: The motel manager wants job applications in a chat with his vending-machine guy. ‘It’s encrypted,’ he says. Excellent. Only authorized strangers can read your address.

choices.label: Check the roster; document the problem

effects.log: You record stray contacts without private details. The vending-machine guy confirms he is not HR.
‘Totally private,’ you tell everyone. A former employee replies, ‘I quit during the Obama administration.’
He lists who may see applications. The housekeeper crosses out ‘everyone in the chat.’ One more mess management expects her to clean.

name: The Public Comment Endurance Test
desc: The hearing on efficiency has spent an hour praising itself. Public comments get three minutes. A cleaner asks whether all that applause is on the clock.

choices.label: Use one snack pack; stay and speak

effects.log: Snacks gone, patience gone, statement recorded. Your three minutes contain more verbs than the chair's hour.

choices.label: Withdraw; walk back to the van

effects.log: You hike back, aching and unheard. The chair records another successful reduction in public complaints.
You miss your turn but recover your patience. The chair thanks the empty microphone for keeping its comments brief.

name: Public Accountability, Folding Chairs
desc: A community screening covers political pressure on weather forecasters. On-screen, nobody remembers who gave the order. The folding chair beneath you has accepted sole responsibility for your suffering.

choices.label: Check the discussion against the investigation

effects.log: The dates line up. The excuses don’t. Your headache has excellent supporting documentation.
You bookmark the discussion and escape the chair. Accountability can continue without conducting experiments on your tailbone.

choices.label: Share a recap from memory; get some sleep

effects.log: You sleep through the correction to your forwarded claim. A perfect cabinet performance, minus the salary.

name: Receipts at the Community Table
desc: A retired bookkeeper checks DOGE’s billion-to-million correction. She counts six biscuits onto a plate. “Six thousand, if anyone from Washington asks.”

choices.label: Use your paper; share checked examples

effects.log: Copies made, checked notes saved. The biscuit tin survives its audit without requiring a spokesperson.
The totals finally add up. Somebody checks the calculator for a deep-state switch.
Your total gets corrected. Congratulations: you've brought federal accounting standards to the neighborhood.

name: Fundraiser Detour
desc: The fundraiser's corporate sponsor sent a six-foot logo. Nobody brought a pan big enough to cook it. Guests who can spare food are supplying dinner.

effects.log: You supply actual food. The organizer puts your names above the company that donated a JPEG.
You skip the speeches. The engine makes fewer promises and is noticeably easier to interrupt.

name: Corporate Says It’s Healthy
desc: A wellness booth offers free raw milk, wrapped snacks, and MAHA-themed ‘bodily freedom.’ The attendant has a script, research links, and corporate instructions on the correct angle of her smile.

effects.log: Your stomach begins its own review. The next exit becomes the only policy issue that matters.
The cited study isn’t about milk. You show the attendant. Corporate’s science joins the recycling.
You stash the snacks. Their ingredients list fits on the wrapper without a presidential commission.

name: Tariff Whiplash
desc: A new tariff list demands extra spares for your signed parts trade. Corporate’s “Remain Positive” email supplies the clerk’s script: “Unfortunately, unfortunately, unfortunately.”

choices.label: Check terms; trade two supply packs

effects.log: Two packs gone; surcharge documented. Your signature apparently approved whatever number came next.

choices.label: Claim the extra pack was included

effects.log: You get the extra pack and lose the benefit of the doubt. Management material.

choices.label: Compare slips; offer one supply pack

effects.log: One pack accepted, corrected terms saved. Corporate's positive-attitude email survives every revision.

name: Has Anyone Tried Paying the Rent?
desc: At a housing meeting, a council member prescribes healthier choices using the MAHA report. A tenant asks whether her landlord counts as a parasite. He turns off her microphone.

choices.label: Wait your turn to read the rent figures

effects.log: Standing wears you out. You read the posted rents aloud; he cuts the mic. The room is now officially affordable.
Your legs ache. A tenant suggests listing the council member on Airbnb: spacious, vacant, difficult to contact.
The quiet helps. Your ‘rents doubled’ claim fails a phone check. You try again, louder.

name: Heartland Waystation
desc: Food-aid drivers offer their fastest shortcut for help with crates, or an easier route over coffee. 'Deliveries still have to arrive,' one says. 'Unlike the federal food money.'

choices.label: Stack crates; take the fastest shortcut

effects.log: You move the crates and skip the jam. Six workers outmaneuver a planning committee without appointing one.

choices.label: Drink their coffee; take the easier route

effects.log: Coffee improves the directions. The driver narrates the map like the van has acquired a sports commentator.

name: Rust Belt Convoy
desc: Tariff paperwork has parked a line of trucks. Drivers offer a fast back-road group or the marked detour. Their cargo has traveled farther between inboxes.

choices.label: Share a pack; follow the lead

effects.log: Snacks shared, miles gained. The trucker’s “Follow me” is the shortest trade policy you’ve heard all day.
You signal and leave a gap. The trucker approves a trade agreement consisting entirely of waving.

name: The Flagger Knows the Way
desc: A “DOGE SAVINGS” banner hangs over a closed lane. Beneath it, a flagger offers a fast coned route or an easier merge. Both existed before the banner claimed credit.

choices.label: Take the coned route on signal

effects.log: You gain miles. The flagger gets you moving with one hand. The banner requires two poles to stand there.
You merge smoothly. The back-seat transport committee is reduced to one satisfied grunt.

name: No Subscription Required
desc: After a hot drive, a volunteer medic offers a free check and mentions low supplies. Across the street, a booth sells ‘freedom from modern medicine.’ The insurance industry calls that a deductible.

effects.log: You declare everyone fine. Six worried people spend the next mile conducting a medical review by side-eye.

choices.label: Use your water; get checked — 1 supply

effects.log: You drink your water and get checked. The bill is so absent you check under the chair.
Bandages donated, shortages logged. The wellness banner covers twelve square feet and absolutely no wounds.

name: Five Accomplishments, Six Exhausted People
desc: It’s midnight outside the hearing hall. Your comment on five-accomplishment reports is stuck in a six-person fight over commas. The lot attendant offers to text when the doors open.

choices.label: Keep everyone awake; finish the notes

effects.log: The notes grow longer. The van becomes an unpaid staff meeting with worse ventilation.

choices.label: Share one pack; take turns working

effects.log: One supply pack buys rotating naps. Democracy runs on crackers and whoever's least asleep.
You sleep; your new ally texts when the doors open. The message ends before anyone asks for a campaign donation.

name: Emergency Straw Reserve
desc: Trump’s straw display blocks the water cooler. The cashier offers $10 to count boxes. ‘We’re free,’ she says, ‘to move this shit again.’

effects.log: Six dollars for water, free straws. Washington would like credit for the affordable part.
Ten dollars earned. The manager asks for a second count. Freedom has a closing checklist.
You pass a 'WE LISTENED' banner. Six broke people try to look more like drinking utensils.

name: Five Things Corn Did Last Week
desc: The farmer copied Washington’s five-accomplishment emails. His worker offers you $8 to type four entries. The corn continues growing without submitting supporting documentation.

choices.label: Document the work the form omits

effects.log: You save her approved account, cross-eyed. Management has converted photosynthesis into a clerical backlog.
You type her notes and pocket eight dollars. The corn has hired a ghostwriter.
You leave her filling boxes. Outside, the corn brazenly refuses to network.

name: Locally Grown Funding Gap
desc: The co-op offers twelve bucks to load crates. Since the federal food fund was canceled, the tomatoes have had to develop a fundraising strategy.

effects.log: The co-op swaps contact details with you. Your beans have negotiated better connections than your résumé.
You load the crates and collect twelve dollars. Your back sends its invoice separately.
Back in the van, you discuss incorporating the beans. Maybe then somebody will bail them out.

name: The Cow Hasn’t Read It Either
desc: A dairy stand’s MAHA-style research links are dead. The cardboard cow smiles through it. Corporate has found a spokesperson who can’t request back pay.

choices.label: Check titles; save the dead links

effects.log: You save the mismatches, squinting. The cow remains the only author you can locate.
Five dollars. Two snack packs. The wrappers make no campaign promises.
You leave hungry. The cardboard cow keeps smiling through lunch. Corporate has finally found its model employee.

name: Optimism Will Not Dry Your Socks
desc: A festival promoter covers a rain warning with a sun sticker. A worker points out the shelter. Trump needed a marker; this guy has outsourced meteorology to the craft aisle.

effects.log: You recover over a snack. Outside, the sun sticker makes its first contact with weather.

choices.label: Trust the sign; reassure the crew

effects.log: You relax and announce clear skies. Then the first raindrop performs a hostile fact-check.
You pass the fry stall. Nobody says ‘at least we saved money’ without a death stare.

name: Gulf of Parking Lot
desc: The owner renamed his puddle the Gulf of Premium Parking. He offers you $7 to repaint the sign. The attendant wanted a drain and received an ocean.

effects.log: Seven dollars earned. The owner announces a waterfront upgrade. The attendant resumes asking for a drain.

choices.label: Check and mark the dry exit

effects.log: You mark the dry exit. The owner's maritime empire ends at a correctly drawn arrow.
You leave the puddle undefeated. The van's cup holder remains your entire waterfront portfolio.

name: The Minimum Viable Library
desc: A librarian offers $9 for catalog checks while a federal form demands reading’s dollar value. She writes ‘more than this form.’ Invalid currency.

effects.log: The librarian gives you her contact card. Your crackers now qualify as a suspiciously effective public-private partnership.
Nine dollars earned and a librarian's endorsement. Your eyes would like books to come in fewer letters.
You pass the free-computer sign. Dangerous stuff. Somebody could look up what a union does.

name: The Tariff Relabeling Shift
desc: Another tariff update. The dispatcher offers fourteen dollars to move boxes, two supply packs to match labels. “We're bringing jobs back. From that pallet to this pallet.”

effects.log: Fourteen dollars earned. Your shoulders would like to offshore the next box.

choices.label: Match labels for two supply packs

effects.log: Cross-eyed, you collect two road packs. You check whether lunch has also been amended.
The boxes stay. So does the gas-money problem.

name: The Patriotic Parts Counter
desc: The TV says China pays the tariffs. The cashier turns the $12 card reader toward you.

effects.log: You buy the kit. China owes you a beer.
She prints it. “For your reimbursement from China.”
The kit stays on the shelf, awaiting payment from Beijing.

name: The Eight-Billion-Dollar Pothole
desc: DOGE listed an $8 million contract as $8 billion. A diner owner offers $10 to haul pothole patch. “I checked my math.”

effects.log: You save both. A cashier has to explain a missing quarter. DOGE gets three spare zeroes.
You haul the bags and pocket $10. Your back would prefer DOGE’s math.
Finally, a problem you can solve by moving further left.

name: Please Account for the Bridge
desc: The bridge supervisor demands five accomplishments. The workers have listed every repair. Their report comes back: “More impact.” One points down at the river.

choices.label: Type, check and save their report

effects.log: Report saved, eyes aching. “Kept the cars out of the river” is somehow the difficult part to explain.
Your new ally submits “chewed” five times on the wrapper. Lunch now qualifies as more productive than bridge repair.
You cross the bridge. Its workers are still explaining why that should count.

name: Reply All, Clock Out
desc: A café chat mixes lunch orders with staff messages. A customer asks whether ‘unpaid close’ comes with fries. The cashier offers eight dollars to sort the customer contacts from the staff.

effects.log: You show the owner. He creates separate chats and calls it a restructuring.
Eight dollars. Forty-seven messages. The owner describes identifying three customers as ‘digital transformation.’
You leave without eight dollars. The gas pump has no interest in your work-life balance.

name: Hydration Sovereignty
desc: The truck stop’s Trump showerhead promotion has soaked its LIMITED GOVERNMENT banner. The clerk offers $9 to hold the stand steady. Free showers require your own soap and considerably less patriotism.

effects.log: You emerge clean. The crew declines your suggestion of a ribbon-cutting for the armpits.
Nine dollars and aching arms for holding the display upright. The clerk admires the design: 'Saved a fortune on the base.'
You leave unwashed. The van's air freshener submits a resignation letter.

name: The Exhibit of Pending Funds
desc: The museum offers $11 to scan photos while it waits for federal funding. 'We exhibit starvation wages,' says the guide. 'We’re not supposed to demonstrate them.'

effects.log: You finish the scans and collect eleven dollars. The historical payroll is starting to look competitive.

choices.label: Share one snack bundle; take tour

effects.log: The guide shares your snacks beside the company-store exhibit. Your employer's discount scheme suddenly looks less original.
The exhibit ends at the eight-hour day. Your phone asks whether you'd like to work tonight.

name: Click Here for Fifteen Dollars
desc: An editor offers fifteen dollars to check MAHA’s citations. ‘Can you open a link?’ she asks. You finally encounter a job requirement the report’s authors could not meet.

effects.log: Fifteen dollars earned. Mismatches logged. Your eyes have put in for hazard pay.

choices.label: Vouch for the studies by title

effects.log: Your cabinet impression gets a laugh. The editor opens a link: wrong paper. ‘Oh. You’re still doing the impression.’
You decline. The fuel gauge immediately requests a meeting about your career choices.

name: The Shelf Is Still Hungry
desc: The federal food fund vanished. The forms reproduced. A co-op volunteer offers work: 'Backache pays in groceries. Headache pays cash.'

choices.label: Pack bags for three food bundles

effects.log: Three bundles earned. Your shoulders would like their share delivered directly to a heating pad.
Ten dollars for matching groceries to addresses. Add a subscription fee and a tech founder could announce he invented delivery.
You keep driving. For dinner, the government recommends imagining how much worse socialism would taste.

name: Manager Approval Required
desc: A server on break scrolls through the cabinet’s leaked airstrike chat. “They invited a journalist. I need a manager’s PIN to refund ranch.”

effects.log: You save it. Apparently you’re cleared for airstrikes, just not dipping sauce.
The crew laughs. You invent a detail, then defend it. Now you’re doing the whole administration.
Two minutes for fries, then back to guarding the strategic ranch reserve.

name: The Name Is the Infrastructure
desc: The visitor desk’s $6 map shows a grandly renamed bridge, open to traffic. Outside, it’s closed. A clerk draws the detour by hand. The county has rebuilt the map.

effects.log: You keep it beside the closure notice. Six dollars for the county’s collectible alternate reality.
You untangle the notices and save the route. The clerk christens your headache “Progress.” It continues hurting.

choices.label: Leave and follow the posted detour

effects.log: You take the detour. The ribbon-cutting photo remains the shortest route across the river.

name: Strategic Straw Inspection
desc: A stand owner filming 'straw inspections' waves you into his video. His cashier says Trump's order covers federal purchasing. He requests fewer facts. She's still waiting for her break.

choices.label: Give cashier one snack; decline video

effects.log: She eats your snack on camera. 'I'd like my break now.' His freedom documentary has accidentally acquired a labor demand.

choices.label: Read and save the actual order

effects.log: You save the order and correct him on camera. He asks whether facts come in plastic.
He films another take. Your cup has received more scrutiny than a defense contract.

name: The National Shower Demonstration
desc: The Trump showerhead demonstration is flooding the sandwich stand. The manager offers twelve bucks to mop. Five buys a shower that hasn't annexed lunch.

effects.log: You mop until your back aches and collect twelve dollars. The manager announces that the system is 'self-draining.'
You get clean for five dollars. The water stays in the shower. The manager calls this 'nothing special.'
The manager promises another demonstration. The cleaner begins moving sandwiches to higher ground.

name: The Museum of Very Large Savings
desc: A DOGE exhibit offers $13 to check labels against sources. Beside the billion-to-million correction sits a quarter labeled “One Trillion, Pending Review.”

effects.log: Notes saved, head aching, $13 collected. Counting it twice fails to produce $26. You’re clearly unqualified for DOGE.
The crew laughs until you repeat the wrong figure. The curator adds you to the correction.
You leave the quarter's promotion ceremony. Your own net worth remains offensively well documented.

name: The Ribbon-Cutting Holding Pattern
desc: At a display about Chicago’s paused transit funds, organizers offer $9 to tally surveys. A cleaner eyes the ceremonial ribbon. ‘Try cutting my commute.’

effects.log: Volunteers add your number beside the survey hotline. Your contribution is listed under 'edible infrastructure.'
Nine dollars and a headache. One nurse lists 'my manager's imagination' under alternative transportation.
You drive away. The ribbon remains a zero-emissions vehicle with an exceptionally limited range.

name: Six Dollars for Better Weather
desc: A vendor offers six dollars to replace a rain warning with ‘Clear skies ahead.’ He cites Trump’s hurricane map. No forecasting experience required. Eyesight discouraged.

choices.label: Save the sign and official forecast

effects.log: You document the mismatch until your eyes ache. The vendor asks whether facts require a permit.
You pocket six dollars. A worker checks their forecast app. Your meteorology career ends at orientation.
You keep your integrity. The gas pump regrets it does not participate in that rewards program.

name: This Reference Needs a Pulse
desc: The clinic offers $12 to check corrected MAHA references and treatment from your kit. “Washington makes a typo, I lose lunch,” says the receptionist.

effects.log: Twelve dollars and a saved correction list. Your brain now displays ‘This page is not responding.’

choices.label: Accept care using your kit — 1 supply

effects.log: The nurse uses your kit and you recover. She opens the bandages without making you choose a subscription tier.
The van’s second opinion is ‘probably fine.’ Opinions three through six have nothing to add.

name: Patriotic Thesaurus
desc: A coastal grant writer offers paid work translating the same public project into language that will survive Trump’s grant review. The sidewalk is now a freedom corridor. The shade tree is awaiting clearance.

effects.log: You earn twelve dollars. The project is unchanged; its adjectives have passed inspection.
You preserve the original and the patriotic translation. The receipts need no translation.
The crew leaves the offer behind.

name: High-Speed Replacement Van
desc: After another Trump rail-funding fight, a contractor proposes replacing high-speed rail with vans and motivational language. Their ribbon-cutting team has transportation needs of its own.

effects.log: You collect fifteen dollars. Your van is now the most operational part of the announcement.
A commuter joins your contacts. The brochure’s dotted line is still not a railway.
The crew leaves the offer behind.

name: A Building Is Overhead
desc: A mountain-region laboratory is preparing for Trump’s proposed NIH overhead cap. The budget funds the experiment but objects to walls, power and refrigeration. A researcher offers you a practical choice.

effects.log: Fourteen dollars earned. You confirm the freezer is an essential scientific instrument, not a lifestyle choice.
The research crew returns the favor with basic care and a new contact.
The crew leaves the offer behind.

name: Wind Loyalty Hearing
desc: Following Trump’s order against wind and solar subsidies, a roadside energy fair is judging whether the breeze is sufficiently patriotic. A technician needs help that will actually keep equipment working.

effects.log: Ten dollars earned. The wind keeps generating power without completing its loyalty questionnaire.
You gain a contact and an explanation involving actual electricity.
The crew leaves the offer behind.

name: Desert Shower Freedom
desc: A desert service stop celebrates Trump’s shower-pressure order with a demonstration nobody budgeted water for. The plumber offers to end the ceremony before the tank runs dry.

effects.log: You leave with water and a working understanding of the off switch.
Twelve dollars earned. Working under the sink is less comfortable than announcing freedom above it.
The crew leaves the offer behind.

name: America First, Argentina Next
desc: Trump’s idea to import more Argentine beef has reached a cattle-country loading yard. The ranchers are comparing the America First speeches with the import paperwork. The manifest needs a second pair of eyes.

effects.log: Sixteen dollars earned. The cattle’s country of origin is clearer than the policy’s.

choices.label: Compare the speeches with the receipts

effects.log: You add the contradiction to your evidence file. Nobody has yet asked the cows to apologize.
The crew leaves the offer behind.
